title: Crypto Dashboard Overview
description: What you can do from the main crypto dashboard
content: The Yativo Crypto dashboard (crypto.yativo.com) is your main hub for managing crypto wallets, WaaS accounts, virtual cards, gift cards, and developer tools. From the sidebar you can navigate to: Accounts (wallet balances and addresses), Transactions (full history), Swap (exchange tokens), Cards (virtual and physical cards), Agentic Wallets (automated wallets), Virtual Accounts (IBAN), Payment Gateway, Gift Cards, Payouts, Customers (WaaS), Developer (API keys and webhooks), and Subscriptions. The top bar shows your current balance summary and notification bell. Dark mode can be toggled from the profile menu at the top right.

title: Viewing Wallet Accounts and Balances
description: How to view your crypto wallet accounts and balances on the dashboard
content: Go to Accounts in the sidebar to see all your crypto wallets. Each wallet card shows the asset (e.g. USDC, EURC), the network (Ethereum, Solana, Tron, etc.), your current balance, and the wallet address. Click any wallet to see its deposit address and QR code for receiving funds. You can copy the address with one click. To create a new wallet, click 'Add Account' and select the asset and network. If a balance shows as 0 but you expect funds, check the correct network — for example USDC on Solana is a different wallet from USDC on Ethereum.

title: Sending Cryptocurrency
description: Step-by-step guide to sending crypto from the dashboard
content: To send crypto: 1) Go to Accounts and click the wallet you want to send from. 2) Click 'Send'. 3) Enter the recipient wallet address — double-check the network matches (sending USDC on Ethereum to a Solana address will fail). 4) Enter the amount. 5) Review the network fee shown — this is deducted from your wallet. 6) Confirm. For large amounts, the transaction may require extra confirmation. If the send button is greyed out, your balance is too low to cover the amount plus network fees. Transaction status goes: Pending → Processing → Complete (or Failed). Most transactions complete within 1-5 minutes depending on network congestion.

title: Receiving Cryptocurrency
description: How to get your deposit address and receive crypto
content: To receive crypto: 1) Go to Accounts and find the wallet for the asset you want to receive (e.g. USDC on Solana). 2) Click the wallet to expand it. 3) Your deposit address is shown along with a QR code — share either with the sender. Always confirm the network with the sender before sharing the address. Deposits are credited automatically once the transaction has enough confirmations on-chain (usually 1-3 blocks). If a deposit is not showing after 30 minutes, check the transaction hash on a block explorer to confirm it was sent to the correct address and network.

title: Swapping Tokens on the Dashboard
description: How to exchange one crypto asset for another using the Swap page
content: To swap tokens: 1) Click Swap in the sidebar. 2) Select the asset you want to sell (From) and the asset you want to receive (To). 3) Enter the amount. 4) A live quote is fetched showing the exchange rate and estimated output. 5) Quotes expire in 30 seconds — if yours expires, refresh to get a new one. 6) Click 'Confirm Swap'. The swap settles in seconds to minutes. Swap rates include a small spread. If you see 'Insufficient balance', ensure your source wallet has enough to cover the swap amount. You cannot swap between the same asset on different networks (e.g. USDC Solana to USDC Ethereum) — use bridging for that, which is not currently supported in-dashboard.

title: Viewing and Filtering Transaction History
description: How to view, search, and export your crypto transaction history
content: Go to Transactions in the sidebar to see all activity across your wallets. You can filter by: date range, asset, network, transaction type (send/receive/swap/fee), and status (pending/complete/failed). Click any transaction row to see the full details including the blockchain hash. To look up a transaction on-chain, copy the hash and paste it into the block explorer for that network (e.g. Solscan for Solana, Etherscan for Ethereum). Transaction statuses: Pending = waiting for on-chain confirmation; Processing = detected on chain; Complete = fully confirmed; Failed = rejected by the network. Failed transactions do not charge fees unless gas was consumed.

title: Virtual Cards — Creating, Funding, and Using
description: How to create and manage virtual cards on the crypto dashboard
content: Go to Cards in the sidebar to manage virtual cards. To create a card: click 'Create Card', choose Individual or Company, fill in the details, and complete any required verification. Once created, fund the card by transferring from your crypto wallet — the balance converts to USD. To view card details (card number, CVV, expiry): click the card and select 'Reveal Details'. Use the card for online purchases wherever Visa/Mastercard is accepted. If a card is declined, check: (1) sufficient balance, (2) the merchant doesn't block virtual cards, (3) the card is active and not frozen. You can freeze/unfreeze a card instantly from the card detail screen.

title: Agentic Wallets — What They Are and How to Use Them
description: Understanding and managing agentic wallets from the dashboard
content: Agentic Wallets are programmable wallets that can execute crypto transactions automatically based on rules or triggers — useful for business flows, payroll, recurring payments, or AI-driven operations. To create one: go to Agentic Wallets in the sidebar and click 'Create Wallet'. Give it a name and optionally configure spending rules. Each agentic wallet has its own address per network. You can fund it from your main account, monitor its transaction history, and set up webhooks to be notified of activity. Agentic wallets can be connected to external systems via API. If you need to stop all activity, use the 'Pause' button on the wallet detail screen.

title: Gas Station — Auto-Funding Network Fees
description: How the gas station works and how to manage it
content: The Gas Station automatically tops up your wallets with native tokens (ETH, SOL, MATIC, etc.) to cover network fees, so your users never have to manage gas manually. Go to Accounts → Gas Station to configure it. You set a minimum threshold — when a wallet's native balance falls below this, the Gas Station deposits a top-up. The Gas Station deducts from your main balance. You can enable/disable it per network and adjust the top-up amount. If transactions are failing with 'insufficient gas', check that the Gas Station is active and has sufficient reserve funds. View gas usage history in the Gas Station tab.

title: Virtual Accounts (IBAN) — Receiving Bank Transfers
description: How to create and use IBAN virtual accounts to receive bank transfers
content: Virtual Accounts let you receive bank wire transfers (EUR via SEPA, GBP via Faster Payments, etc.) directly into your Yativo account. Go to Virtual Accounts in the sidebar. To create one: click 'Create Account', select the currency, and complete any required KYC. You get a unique IBAN and BIC to share with senders. Incoming transfers typically arrive within 1-2 business days (SEPA) or the same day (Faster Payments). Once received, funds appear in your wallet balance. Transfers can only be received from accounts in the name of your registered business. If a transfer is returned, check that the sender's name matches your KYC details.

title: Gift Cards — Purchasing and Redeeming
description: How to buy gift cards using your crypto balance
content: Go to Gift Cards in the sidebar to browse and buy prepaid gift cards (Amazon, iTunes, Google Play, gaming cards, and more) using your crypto balance. Select a brand, choose the denomination, and click Buy. The card code is delivered immediately to your email and shown in the dashboard. Gift cards are non-refundable once purchased. If a code doesn't work at the retailer: check the correct region (US cards may not work outside the US), ensure the balance hasn't already been used, and contact support if the issue persists. Purchases are deducted from your USDC or USDT balance.

title: KYC / Identity Verification on the Crypto Dashboard
description: How to complete identity verification and what to do if it fails
content: KYC (Know Your Customer) verification unlocks higher transaction limits and additional features. To start: go to Profile Settings → Verification or follow the banner prompt. You'll need to provide: government-issued photo ID (passport or national ID), a selfie, and for business accounts, company registration documents. The review typically takes 1-24 hours. If rejected: the rejection reason is shown in your profile — common reasons are blurry documents, expired ID, or name mismatch. Re-submit with corrected documents. While pending, you can still use basic features but sending limits are reduced. Approved status is permanent unless your documents expire.

title: Managing API Keys on the Crypto Dashboard
description: How to create, scope, and rotate API keys
content: Go to Developer → API Keys to manage your API credentials. To create a key: click 'Generate Key', give it a name, select the permission scopes it needs (e.g. wallets:read, transactions:write), optionally set an expiry and IP allowlist, then click Create. The API secret is shown only once — copy it immediately to a secure location. If you lose the secret, you must rotate the key (delete and recreate). To rotate: click the key row, select Rotate or Delete, then create a new one. Your API key is used to get a Bearer token via POST /api/v1/auth/token. Never expose your API secret in client-side code or public repositories.

title: Setting Up Webhooks on the Crypto Dashboard
description: How to configure webhook endpoints to receive real-time event notifications
content: Go to Developer → Webhooks to configure event notifications. Click 'Add Endpoint', enter your HTTPS URL, and select the events to subscribe to (e.g. transaction.completed, wallet.funded). Yativo signs every webhook with a secret — verify the X-Yativo-Signature header in your server to confirm authenticity. To test: use the 'Send Test Event' button which delivers a sample payload to your endpoint. If webhooks are not arriving, check: (1) your endpoint returns a 2xx status within 10 seconds, (2) there's no firewall blocking Yativo's IPs, (3) the endpoint URL is publicly reachable (not localhost). Failed deliveries are retried 3 times with exponential backoff. View delivery logs in the Webhooks tab.

title: Security Settings — 2FA and Session Management
description: How to enable 2FA and manage account security
content: Go to Security in the sidebar to manage account security. To enable 2FA: click 'Enable Two-Factor Authentication', scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.), and enter the 6-digit code to confirm. Save your backup codes in a secure place — these let you regain access if you lose your authenticator. With 2FA enabled, every login requires your email OTP plus the authenticator code. If you're locked out: use a backup code on the login screen. To disable 2FA: go to Security and toggle it off, then confirm with your current 2FA code. Active sessions are also listed here — you can terminate any session remotely.

title: Subscriptions and Plans
description: How to view, upgrade, or manage your Yativo subscription plan
content: Go to Subscriptions in the sidebar to view your current plan and available upgrades. Each plan tier unlocks different transaction limits, API rate limits, and features (e.g. card issuance, agentic wallets, higher auto-forwarding limits). To upgrade: select a plan and click Subscribe — billing is monthly and charged to your Yativo wallet balance. If your balance is insufficient, the upgrade will fail. Downgrading is effective at the end of the current billing cycle. If you believe you are on the wrong plan or have been charged incorrectly, contact support with your account ID and the relevant billing period.

title: WaaS Customers — Managing End-Users
description: How to create and manage WaaS customer wallets from the dashboard
content: Go to Customers in the sidebar to manage your Wallet-as-a-Service (WaaS) end-users. Each customer record represents a user in your app who has wallets managed by Yativo on your behalf. From here you can: view a customer's wallets and balances, see their transaction history, create wallets for new customers, and check their compliance/KYC status. To create a customer manually: click 'Add Customer', fill in the external ID and email, and assign wallet networks. Most WaaS customers are created programmatically via the API. If a customer's wallet isn't showing a balance they expect, check the correct network and use the transaction hash to verify on a block explorer.

title: Fiat Dashboard Overview (app.yativo.com)
description: What you can do from the main Yativo fiat dashboard
content: The Yativo fiat dashboard (app.yativo.com) serves B2B businesses that need to move money across borders. From the sidebar: Dashboard (balance overview and recent activity), Transactions (full history), Send Money (initiate payouts), Recipients (manage beneficiaries), Virtual Accounts (receive bank transfers), Customers (end-user management), Cards (virtual cards), Swap (currency exchange), Developer (API keys and webhooks), Team (user management), and Profile (account settings). The top bar shows your available balance per currency. All actions that move money require KYC approval — if you see a KYC gate overlay, complete the verification steps first.

title: Sending Money — Step by Step
description: How to send a fiat payout from the dashboard
content: To send money: 1) Click Send Money in the sidebar. 2) Select a saved recipient or add a new one — you need their bank account details (account number, bank, country). 3) Enter the amount and select the source currency. A live exchange rate is shown if sending to a different currency. 4) Add a payment reference (required for some corridors). 5) Review the fee and estimated delivery time. 6) Click Confirm. Transfers typically arrive within minutes (mobile money) to 1-2 business days (bank transfer) depending on the country and payment rail. If a transfer fails, the funds are returned to your wallet within 24 hours. Always double-check recipient bank details before confirming — errors may cause delays.

title: Managing Recipients / Beneficiaries
description: How to add, edit, and manage saved recipients for payouts
content: Go to Recipients in the sidebar to manage your saved payout beneficiaries. To add a new recipient: click 'Add Recipient', select the destination country, enter the recipient's full name, select the payment method (bank transfer, mobile money, etc.), and fill in the account details. Required fields vary by country — for Nigeria you need the account number and bank name; for Mexico, CLABE; for Brazil, PIX key or bank account; for Europe, IBAN. Once added, recipients are saved for future sends. To edit a recipient, click their row and update the details. If a transfer is rejected due to invalid account details, update the recipient record and retry.

title: Virtual Accounts — Receiving Funds via Bank Transfer
description: How to create and use virtual accounts to receive payments
content: Go to Virtual Accounts in the sidebar to get dedicated bank account numbers for receiving funds. Click 'Create Account', select the currency (EUR, GBP, USD, MXN, BRL, NGN), and complete any required verification. You receive a unique account number (IBAN for EUR/GBP, local routing details for other currencies) to share with payers. Incoming transfers credit your Yativo wallet automatically — usually within minutes for mobile money and same day or next day for bank wires. You can create multiple virtual accounts (e.g. one per client or project). If an expected payment hasn't arrived, share the sender's reference or transfer confirmation with support so we can trace it.

title: Business KYC / KYB Verification
description: How to complete business verification to unlock full platform access
content: Business KYC (KYB) is required before making transfers or using API features. If you see a KYC gate blocking the dashboard, click 'Complete Verification'. You'll need to provide: business registration certificate, proof of address for the business, ID documents for the business owner/UBOs (Ultimate Beneficial Owners), and your business website or description. The review takes 1-3 business days. Rejection reasons are shown in the verification section — common issues are expired documents, mismatched business names, or missing UBO information. If your application has been pending more than 3 business days without an update, contact support with your account ID.

title: Virtual Cards on the Fiat Dashboard
description: How to create, fund, and manage virtual cards
content: Go to Cards → Virtual Cards in the sidebar. To create a card: click 'Create Card', enter a label and the initial funding amount. Cards are denominated in USD. To fund an existing card: click the card and select 'Add Funds', then enter the amount to transfer from your wallet. To view card details (number, CVV, expiry): click 'Reveal Details'. Cards can be used for online purchases globally where Visa is accepted. To freeze a card: click the card and toggle Freeze — this blocks all transactions instantly. If a card charge fails, check: sufficient card balance, card is not frozen, and the merchant accepts virtual Visa cards.

title: Currency Swap on the Fiat Dashboard
description: How to exchange between currencies in your Yativo wallet
content: Go to Swap in the sidebar to exchange between currencies in your wallet. Select the source currency (e.g. USD) and the target currency (e.g. NGN or MXN). Enter the amount and click 'Get Quote'. A real-time rate is displayed with the exchange fee included. Click 'Confirm Swap' to execute — swaps settle instantly in your wallet. Rates are valid for 30 seconds; if the quote expires, click Refresh. If the Confirm button is disabled, check that your source wallet has sufficient balance. Swap history is available in the Transactions section filtered by type = Swap.

title: Bulk Transfers — Sending to Many Recipients at Once
description: How to use the bulk send feature to pay multiple recipients in one go
content: Go to Send Money → Bulk Send to pay multiple recipients in a single batch. Download the CSV template, fill in: recipient name, bank details, amount, and currency for each row. Upload the completed CSV. The dashboard validates each row — rows with errors are highlighted with the specific issue (e.g. invalid account number, unsupported country). Fix errors and re-upload. Once validated, review the total amount and click Confirm. Bulk sends are processed sequentially — each payout is independent, so a failure for one recipient does not affect others. Results (success/failure per row) are downloadable after processing. Maximum 500 rows per bulk send.

title: API Keys on the Fiat Dashboard
description: How to find your Account ID and App Secret for API access
content: Go to Developer → API Key in the sidebar to find your API credentials. Your Account ID is shown at the top — this is your stable identifier. To generate an App Secret: click 'Generate Secret'. The secret is shown once only — copy it immediately. Use your Account ID and App Secret to authenticate via POST /api/v1/auth/login which returns a Bearer token. If you lose your App Secret, click Regenerate to create a new one (this invalidates the old secret immediately — any services using the old secret will stop working until updated). The sandbox environment uses different credentials from production — go to the sandbox dashboard at smtp.yativo.com for sandbox keys.

title: Webhooks on the Fiat Dashboard
description: How to configure webhook endpoints for real-time payment notifications
content: Go to Developer → Webhooks to receive real-time notifications when transactions occur. Click 'Add Webhook', enter your HTTPS endpoint URL, and select the events to subscribe to (e.g. payout.completed, deposit.received, card.transaction). Each delivery includes a signature header — verify it using your webhook secret to confirm the payload is from Yativo. If webhooks are not reaching your server: confirm the URL is publicly accessible, your server responds with HTTP 200-299 within 10 seconds, and no firewall is blocking the request. Failed deliveries are retried automatically. View the delivery log under each webhook entry — you can see the response status and payload for each attempt.

title: Team Management — Adding and Managing Users
description: How to invite team members and manage their access
content: Go to Team in the sidebar (account owner only) to manage who has access to your Yativo dashboard. To invite a team member: click 'Invite Member', enter their email, and select their role. Roles: Admin (full access except billing and team management), Finance (send money, view transactions, manage recipients), Developer (API keys, webhooks, read-only transactions), Viewer (read-only access to transactions and balances). Invitees receive an email to set up their account. To remove a member: click their row and select Remove. Team members cannot see or change your API secret. If a team member loses access, check their invitation status — expired invitations must be resent.

title: Tracking a Transaction Status
description: How to track the status of a fiat payout or deposit
content: Go to Transactions in the sidebar and find your transfer — use filters for date, type, or currency to narrow down. Click the transaction row to see full details including the current status and timestamps. Status meanings: Pending = submitted but not yet processed; Processing = sent to the payment network; Completed = funds delivered to recipient; Failed = rejected (reason shown in details); Refunded = failed and returned to your wallet. For bank transfers, 'Processing' may last 1-2 business days. If a transfer shows Processing for more than 2 business days, contact support with the transaction ID. You can also share a public tracking link with the recipient — click 'Share Tracking Link' on the transaction detail screen.

title: Depositing Funds into Your Wallet
description: How to top up your Yativo fiat wallet balance
content: To add funds to your Yativo wallet: 1) Use a Virtual Account — go to Virtual Accounts, get your dedicated bank account number, and wire funds from your bank. This is the recommended method for regular top-ups. 2) For crypto-to-fiat: if you have a crypto wallet, use the Swap feature to convert crypto to fiat. Deposits via virtual account typically arrive same day (mobile money) or 1-2 business days (bank wire). Your wallet balance updates automatically when funds clear. If a deposit is not reflected after the expected time, share the bank transfer receipt or transaction reference with support so the team can trace and credit it manually.

title: Understanding Transaction Statuses
description: What each transaction status means across both dashboards
content: Transaction statuses across Yativo: Pending — the transaction has been created but not yet submitted to the payment network or blockchain. Processing / Confirming — the transaction has been submitted and is waiting for network confirmation or banking processing. Completed / Confirmed — the transaction has been fully processed and funds have been delivered. Failed — the transaction was rejected. The reason is shown in the transaction details (e.g. insufficient balance, invalid account, compliance hold). No funds are lost on failure — they are returned to your wallet. Refunded — a previously completed transaction has been reversed and funds returned. For crypto: a transaction that is Pending for more than 30 minutes may be stuck — check the blockchain status using the transaction hash.

title: Login Issues and Account Access
description: What to do if you cannot log in to your Yativo account
content: Yativo uses passwordless email login — you enter your email and receive a one-time code. If the OTP email doesn't arrive: check your spam folder, ensure you're using the exact email address registered on the account, and wait up to 2 minutes before requesting another code. If you have 2FA enabled and lost access to your authenticator app, use one of your saved backup codes on the login screen. If you've lost all backup codes, contact support with proof of identity. Session expires after inactivity — if you're redirected to the login page unexpectedly, simply log in again. If your account appears suspended, contact support — this may be due to a compliance review or unusual activity.

title: How to Contact Yativo Support
description: How to get human support for urgent or unresolved issues
content: For issues that Yativo AI cannot resolve: visit yativo.com and use the Support chat, or email support@yativo.com with your account ID, a description of the issue, and any relevant transaction IDs or screenshots. For urgent issues (e.g. stuck funds, account suspension, compliance hold), mark your email as URGENT in the subject line. Support is available Monday to Friday during business hours. For API integration issues, include your request payload and the error response you received. Response times: email support typically responds within 1 business day; urgent cases are escalated faster.
